title: Vanishing integral of the closed Gaussian profile
statement: Let $n\ge0$ and let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable. For $u_\theta(x)=\int 1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$, the integral $\int U(u_\theta(x))\,d\gamma_n(x)$ tends to $0$ as $\theta\to0$, where $U(\alpha)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(\alpha))$ for $0<\alpha<1$ and $U(\alpha)=0$ otherwise, with $\varphi$ and $\Phi$ the standard Gaussian density and distribution function.
replaced: Let $\Phi,\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and let $\overline I(p)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$, with $\overline I(p)=0$ elsewhere. Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For a measurable $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, let $u_\theta(x)=\mathbb E_Y1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,Y)$ with $Y\sim\gamma_n$, and put $R_A(\theta)=\Pr(1_A(X)\ne1_A(\cos\theta\,X+\sin\theta\,Y))$ for independent $X,Y\sim\gamma_n$. Then $\int\overline I(u_\theta(x))\,d\gamma_n(x)\to0$ as $\theta\to0$ through real values.
